---
title: "PARI/GP in Quarto"
engine: pari-gp
---

`PARI-GP-ENGINE` lets you put [PARI/GP](https://pari.math.u-bordeaux.fr/) code
in a Quarto document, run it, and show the results — with the code highlighted
properly.

Everything on this site is rendered by the extension itself. The block below is
real code that ran when this page was built:

```{gp}
p = nextprime(10^40)
factor(p - 1)
```

## Install

```bash
quarto add oeistools/PARI-GP-ENGINE
```

You need [Quarto](https://quarto.org) 1.9 or newer and the `gp` executable on
your `PATH`. See [Get started](getting-started.qmd).

## What you get

**Execution.** ` ```{gp} ` cells run in one `gp` session per document, so state
carries from cell to cell, exactly as it would at the `gp` prompt.

**Highlighting.** A syntax definition covering all 1200 functions of PARI/GP
2.17, applied automatically — nothing to configure.

**Figures.** Plots exported as SVG become real figures, with captions and
cross-references. See [Figures](figures.qmd).

**Errors that behave.** A PARI/GP error stops the render and tells you which
cell, unless you asked for the error to be part of the document.

## A taste

The class number and regulator of $\mathbb{Q}(\sqrt[3]{2})$:

```{gp}
K = bnfinit(x^3 - 2, 1);
[K.no, K.reg]
```

And because the session persists, its fundamental units are still one cell
away:

```{gp}
K.fu
```
